title: Deprecation tombstone ledger - a retired id must survive its own removal
description:
MPI-514 shipped a deprecated FLAG on models. The gap is what happens AFTER removal: per docs/model-library.md, "the flag disappears with the ModelDef on the release that removes it". So a retired id becomes indistinguishable from a typo, and no accurate message can be written for anything that still references it.

Fix follows a precedent already in the codebase: on removal the model's DEP ENTRIES are kept so _orphanedDepIds in routes/downloadManager.js can still reclaim the weight (see MPI-470, which deprecated wan-22-t2v-high/low but kept their entries). Extend the same idea to a TOMBSTONE LEDGER covering retired model ids, dep ids, AND node classes, each carrying removedIn.

Then: unknown id -> "unknown requirement x" (dev error); tombstoned id -> "x was removed in 1.5" (accurate, actionable). Node classes belong in it too - a Flow can break from an upstream pack bump renaming a class, not only from a model retirement.

MESSAGES ONLY. No shims, no migrations, no compatibility rescue machinery.

CONSUMERS: (1) Flow cards, which must show a disabled card with a named reason rather than failing at Run; (2) the third-party flow validator, so a dev linting locally gets the identical verdict the app will give the user; (3) a flow-breaking-changes section in release notes - retired model/dep ids and renamed node classes - which is what MPI owes devs in exchange for making maintenance their responsibility.

RELATED: MPI-514 (shipped the flag), MPI-507 (PiD -> upscale plugins), MPI-470 (kept deps after deprecation), the community flow packages card.
